name: Line Integral Convolution
desc: Line integral convolution — a fixed noise texture smeared along the streamlines of a drifting divergence-free flow so the whole frame becomes one silky combed fabric of visible flow lines, the convolution kernel phasing in real time so the texture streams without a single particle being drawn; false-colour flow-viz keyed to speed, burnished graphite, oil-black iridescence, hard engraved contour bands, or ironbow thermal.

energy.doc: contrast stretch + colour gain of the convolved texture (the raw smear is low-contrast by nature)

scale.doc: flow feature size — zooms the vector field from fine combing to broad sweeping swirls

speed.doc: field evolution rate + the kernel phase rate that makes the texture stream along the lines

density.doc: convolution length — how far the noise is smeared (short = grainy tooth, long = glassy silk)

swirl.doc: blend from pure curl-noise turbulence toward a coherent global rotation about the anchor

grain.doc: fixed film-grain tooth over the fabric (texture over flat fill)

hue.doc: primary hue anchoring the palette ramp

x.doc: horizontal anchor of the global rotation centre

y.doc: vertical anchor of the global rotation centre

style.doc: aesthetic: speed-mapped false-colour flow-viz / burnished graphite mono / oil-black iridescence / hard engraved contour bands / ironbow thermal

seed.doc: deterministic seed for the input noise texture and the flow field
